name: Bhangra
notes: Bhangra style pack (Doc 04 template, solo-first). Punjab's harvest joy made global: bhangra began as the Vaisakhi harvest dance of Punjabi farmers — celebration of the crop, danced to the dhol's thunder — and its modern journey is one of the great diaspora stories: staged in post-Partition Punjab, carried to the UK where 1980s British-Punjabi bands fused it with electronic music, and turned by the North American diaspora into a massive COLLEGIATE COMPETITION circuit (Bhangra Blowout, Bruin Bhangra and dozens more) where teams train like athletes. Design truths: bhangra is high-knee, high-energy, shoulder-led JOY — the stamina gates are real (a competition set is cardio at altitude); the core vocabulary (the bhangra bounce, jhummar sway, dhamaal arms, kicks and hops) is genuinely solo-trainable and taught openly by Punjabi instructors worldwide; the dhol's chaal rides in this app's Rhythm Trainer; and the culture node keeps the root visible under the spectacle — Vaisakhi, the fields, and the farmers the dance thanks.

seasons.finale: Film yourself clapping and bouncing the chaal through one full dhol track — the swing of the eight, found.
Film the bhangra bounce with shoulders alive — one full song, knees high, joy visible from across a field.
Film jhummar sway, dhamaal arms, and the single-leg hops chained together — clean entries and exits.
Film a two-song set at full energy — the competition minute standard, honestly attempted.
Find bhangra live: a Vaisakhi mela, a Punjabi wedding, a collegiate competition, a diaspora class. The dhol will find you first.

attributes.name: Set stamina L2
attributes.test: two full bhangra tracks of continuous bounce and arms without the knees dropping — competition sets don't pause

attributes.name: High-knee springs L1
attributes.test: 60s of alternating high-knee lifts with soft landings, chest tall — bhangra's engine, warmed and willing

attributes.name: Shoulder bounce L1
attributes.test: 60s of loose alternating shoulder bounces riding a pulse — relaxed, rhythmic, never shrugged

nodes.name: The dhol and the chaal
checkpoints: the dhol — the great two-headed barrel drum — drives bhangra with the chaal: a swung eight-count of deep dhin and sharp ta strokes; it's in this app's Rhythm Trainer
boliyan (called verses) ride over the drum, and the crowd answers — call-and-response is half the party
modern bhangra tracks fuse the dhol with everything from hip hop to EDM; the chaal survives every remix

nodes.name: Reading the set — peaks and releases
checkpoints: a bhangra set builds in waves: verses simmer, the hook explodes, the dhol solo demands everything
competition sets are choreographed cardio — 7-8 minutes at full output; pace like the teams do, peak where the music peaks
the 'hoi hoi' and 'balle balle' calls are yours too — bhangra is danced out loud

nodes.name: Vaisakhi — the harvest under the spectacle
checkpoints: bhangra began as the Vaisakhi harvest dance of Punjabi farmers — joy for the crop brought in, danced in the fields to the dhol
the staged folk form took shape in post-Partition Punjab; the root is agricultural celebration, and the best dancers still move like the harvest is real
Punjab spans a partitioned border; bhangra's joy belongs to Punjabi culture on both sides of it

nodes.name: The diaspora's engine — UK sound, campus circuit
checkpoints: 1980s British-Punjabi bands wired the dhol to synths and drum machines — UK bhangra made the sound global
the North American diaspora built the collegiate competition circuit — Bhangra Blowout, Bruin Bhangra and dozens more, where teams train like athletes and alumni coach the next generation
Punjabi instructors teach open classes worldwide and online — the dance's doors are famously wide; walk in crediting the fields it came from

nodes.name: The Punjabi folk family — giddha, luddi, sammi
checkpoints: 'bhangra' abroad often means ALL Punjabi folk dance, but Punjab holds a family of distinct traditions: giddha (the women's dance of wit and boliyan), luddi (the victory sway), sammi, and jhummar — each with its own music and meaning
collegiate teams increasingly stage giddha and luddi segments with their own names — naming the tradition you're borrowing from is the circuit's best habit; make it yours
when you see a move you love in a mixed set, ask which tradition it came from — the answer is usually a better story than the move

nodes.name: The bhangra bounce
nodes.anchor: the engine — everything rides on it
checkpoints: knees lift high and land soft on the chaal, chest proud, shoulders bouncing loose in answer
the arms live UP — bhangra's default is arms raised, hands often with the first-finger flick
smile like the harvest came in; bhangra performed grim is a contradiction in terms
keep it going through a whole verse before adding anything — the bounce is the sentence everything else punctuates
mistakes: marching with stiff shoulders (the shoulders are half the dance)
landing heavy (high knees, soft feet — the field, not the stomp)

nodes.name: Jhummar — the slow sway
nodes.origin: the jhummar tradition of the Sandal Bar region — bhangra's slower, circling elder
checkpoints: a slower, swaying triple-step with arms carving gentle circles — the moon to the bounce's sun
danced in a slow circle traditionally; solo, let it orbit your spot
the contrast skill: dropping from full bounce into jhummar's calm and back is what makes sets breathe

nodes.name: Dhamaal arms & the big shapes
checkpoints: arms drive overhead in big alternating pumps and circles — reaping, throwing, celebrating shapes with the whole arm
shapes read from the back of a mela: bhangra vocabulary is built to be seen at festival distance
shoulders stay loose inside the big arms; power without tension is the whole trick

nodes.name: Kicks & single-leg hops
checkpoints: single-leg hops with the free leg kicked or crossed, arms up — the showpiece family
land soft, switch legs often; the knees are a career, not a season
chain: bounce → hops → jhummar → bounce, clean seams — that chain is most of a set's grammar
mistakes: hopping through knee pain (bhangra's joy never requires it — switch or rest)

nodes.name: The two-song set — filmed
checkpoints: two tracks back to back: bounce carrying, jhummar for the breath, dhamaal on the hooks, hops on the dhol solo
energy check at the end of song two — the competition standard is joy that outlasts oxygen
call at least one 'balle balle' out loud on camera; silent bhangra is incomplete

nodes.name: The mela
checkpoints: find bhangra live: a Vaisakhi mela (April, worldwide), a Punjabi wedding floor, a collegiate competition's open crowd, a diaspora class
when a live dhol starts, join — bhangra floors pull strangers in as policy
somewhere mid-bounce, remember the fields; the harvest joy is the whole inheritance
